author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory
summary: A read-only page at /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, named in full. All specialties render on one page; the page is reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory at /specialties.html is opened, then every one of them is listed under its stored name.
Given a specialty two veterinarians hold, when the directory is opened, then both are named under it, first name then last name.
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian is named nowhere on the page.
Given the clinic's specialties, when the directory is opened, then all of them are on the one page and no paging control is offered.
Given the directory, when it is opened, then it carries the same navigation every other page carries.
Given any other page of the system, when it is rendered, then it offers no link to the specialty directory.
Edge case 1: a specialty no veterinarian holds is listed with nothing named under it.
Edge case 2: a veterinarian holding several specialties is named under each of them.
Edge case 3: when the clinic knows no specialty, the page opens empty rather than failing.
Edge case 4: specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one.
Edge case 5: specialty and veterinarian names are shown as stored, not translated; the page's own wording is translated like any other page's.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application; NG-2 is unchanged
A navigation entry for the page, or a link to it from any other page
Searching or filtering within the specialty directory
Listing veterinarians who hold no specialty; the page lists specialties, not the roster
notes: REQ-SYS-001 tension resolved narrowly, not overridden: site navigation names the owner and veterinarian areas only, and this page carries that navigation without appearing in it. The PRD prose for REQ-SYS-001 now states that a page navigation does not name is still reachable at its own address. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Two residues recorded in Open Questions rather than decided: the intended ordering key (only stability is bound), and whether a visible entry point follows later. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit. Pre-existing unrelated doctor failure: layout.toml spec_version 0.1.0 vs manifest 0.2.0 (outside this agent's write scope).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is a second read surface inside the existing vet feature package, built from patterns already in force: Repository, Web controller, Value object, and the shared Thymeleaf layout fragment. One adjustment is needed. The page's root noun is Specialty, and the vet aggregate cannot enumerate a specialty no veterinarian holds, so the listing is read from a new SpecialtyRepository over the specialties table and joined in memory with the cached vet collection. Basis: direct read of the five vet-package sources, VetControllerTests, PetTypeRepository, vetList.html, layout.html, messages.properties, and I18nPropertiesSyncTest (no IDE oracle connected; file reads rather than symbol resolution). docs/system-design.md Contracts now carries the three design-ahead rows plus the requirement id on Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository, and the Contracts prose records the unidirectional association, the per-request read model, identifier matching, and the absent second cache.
integration_points: New GET /specialties.html on a new package-private SpecialtyController in the vet package; VetController is left untouched, and its @WebMvcTest(VetController.class) slice stays unaffected

SpecialtyRepository extends org.springframework.data.repository.Repository<Specialty, Integer> with one @Transactional(readOnly = true) query returning every specialty in name order; it exposes no write method
SpecialtyDirectory is assembled from specialtyRepository plus the existing @Cacheable("vets") VetRepository.findAll(), so the page shares the warm vet cache and declares no cache of its own
The template replaces fragments/layout with a menu argument matching no existing menu item, so the page carries site navigation without gaining an entry in it (REQ-SYS-001)
No CacheConfiguration change, no schema change, no seed-data change, no layout.html change

patterns.description: narrow read-only repository over a lookup entity with an explicit ORDER BY name — the shape SpecialtyRepository mirrors; prefer VetRepository's tighter `extends Repository` base over PetTypeRepository's JpaRepository
read-only, cached repository interface confined to the methods the feature needs
controller shape: read, put a named attribute on the Model, return the view name; the specialty page drops the pagination helper entirely
template shape: th:text="#{key}" with an English fallback between the tags, the #{none} key for an empty cell, and the layout fragment replace at the html element
Value object row governs SpecialtyDirectory: immutable, defensive copies, equal by value, no persistence mapping, unit-testable without Spring

risks.risk: Deriving the listing from the vet aggregate (grouping vetRepository.findAll() by specialty) silently drops every specialty no veterinarian holds, failing the first acceptance bullet and edge case 1. The seeded data hides it — all three seeded specialties are held.
risks.mitigation: Read the specialty list from SpecialtyRepository; the vet collection supplies only the names under each. Cover it with a test whose fixture includes an unheld specialty.

risks.risk: Grouping by Specialty object identity. BaseEntity and NamedEntity define no equals/hashCode, and with spring.jpa.open-in-view disabled the cached vets' Specialty instances need not be the instances SpecialtyRepository returns. A Map keyed on Specialty would render every specialty empty.
risks.mitigation: Match on the specialty identifier (getId()) inside SpecialtyDirectory. Do not add equals/hashCode to the shared mapped superclasses for this slice.

risks.risk: Adding an inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy = "specialties") collection of Vet to Specialty. It changes the aggregate shape for one read view and makes the eagerly-fetched association cyclic; the /vets serialization route walks Vet.getSpecialties() and would recurse.
risks.mitigation: Keep the association mapped on Vet alone. The join happens in the read model, which is now recorded in docs/system-design.md § Contracts.

risks.risk: Extending JpaRepository for SpecialtyRepository would expose save and delete on a feature whose non-goal is management (NG-2), against the minimal-surface principle.
risks.mitigation: Extend Repository and declare only the read query.

risks.risk: New message keys must be added to messages.properties and the nine translated bundles (messages_en is intentionally empty and skipped), and I18nPropertiesSyncTest checks key presence, not translation quality — an English placeholder in ten locales passes the test and breaks REQ-LANG-002.
risks.mitigation: Build the page from existing keys where possible: #{specialties}, #{vets}, #{name}, #{none} are already translated everywhere. Any genuinely new key needs a real translation in every bundle.

risks.risk: Hard-coded text in the new template. I18nPropertiesSyncTest walks src/main and fails on literal text between tags without #{ or a th:text attribute.
risks.mitigation: Follow vetList.html exactly: th:text="#{key}" carrying the English fallback as element content.

risks.risk: Putting the grouping inline in the controller. The Web controller row of the pattern catalog admits no rule beyond bind-delegate-select, and the existing controller deviations are explicitly not extended to new code.
risks.mitigation: Assemble in SpecialtyDirectory as a pure static factory over the two collections, and unit-test it without Spring context.

risks.risk: Editing fragments/layout.html to add a navigation entry would break the acceptance bullet forbidding any inbound link, and every other page's test.
risks.mitigation: layout.html is a read-only reference here. The page passes an unmatched menu argument; the absence of a link is asserted by a test over the rendered navigation.

risks.risk: The page reads both tables in full with no paging, by requirement.
risks.mitigation: Accepted at the demonstration's scale (three specialties, six veterinarians) and bounded by NG-2, which leaves no write path to grow either table. No pagination scaffolding is to be added speculatively.

notes: Ordering: the PRD binds stability only and leaves the key open. Use the precedent already in the codebase — specialties by stored name (PetTypeRepository's ORDER BY name, Vet.getSpecialties()'s Comparator), veterinarians by last name then first name — expressed as an explicit ORDER BY or Comparator, never as HashSet iteration order. Changing the key later is one comparator. Divergence from the prd-entry's advisory file_targets: it named VetController and no repository. A separate SpecialtyController matches the naming rule (controller prefixed by the domain noun or surface it serves), matches the owner package's one-controller-per-noun precedent, keeps the existing @WebMvcTest(VetController.class) slice and its Mockito fixtures untouched, and avoids piling a new route onto the controller that still carries the /vets route pending removal. New tests should prefer a hand-written SpecialtyRepository stub over @MockitoBean, per CLAUDE.md's mocking policy; MockMvc remains the sanctioned mock. No ADR written: every new type matches an in-force catalog pattern (Repository, Web controller, Value object), the specialties-table read is forced by the requirement rather than chosen against an alternative, and the unidirectional-association constraint is recorded as current state in docs/system-design.md § Contracts, so no imperative line needs a back-link. No ubiquitous-language addition: 'specialty directory' is a page name like 'veterinarian directory', and both Specialty and Veterinarian are already canonical. Security: read-only GET with no parameters, no new trust boundary, stored names escaped by Thymeleaf's default; NG-1 and the absent access control are unchanged. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit. Pre-existing doctor failure (layout.toml spec_version 0.1.0 vs manifest 0.2.0) is unrelated and outside this agent's write scope.

author: code-quality-reviewer
recommendations: src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html:20-24 — the veterinarian-name cell is built from two sibling <span> elements split awkwardly across lines (the per-vet th:each span self-closes, then a literal space, then the empty-state th:if span starts on the next line); a reader must trace tag boundaries carefully to see there are two independent spans. Names are also joined by a bare trailing space baked into th:text (`firstName + ' ' + lastName + ' '`) rather than a visible separator, so multiple veterinarians render as one run-on string with no delimiter (e.g. 'Helen Leary James Carter'). Consider a comma-or-newline separator and reformatting the two spans onto clearly separate lines for readability.
approved_aspects: SpecialtyRepository correctly extends the narrow Repository marker (no save/delete) with an explicit ORDER BY, mirroring the PetTypeRepository/VetRepository precedent the design block calls for

SpecialtyDirectory is a proper immutable value object: List.copyOf defensive copies in both the outer record and nested Entry, static factory assembly, no persistence mapping, matches held-by-identifier rather than object identity with a clear Javadoc explaining why

SpecialtyController follows the established bind-delegate-select controller shape, stays package-private consistent with VetController, and correctly separates the new route from VetController to avoid disturbing its existing @WebMvcTest slice

Template follows the existing th:text="#{key}" with English fallback convention, layout fragment replace matches vetList.html's pattern, and correctly passes an unmatched menu argument so no navigation entry is added
No get/set prefix violations, no raw Object/Map usage, no swallowed exceptions, no logging concerns, all methods small and single-purpose
docs/system-design.md Contracts rows accurately describe the shipped types and match the code read

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain: no NVD match ran in this review — the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle and the reviewer has no network access. This slice changes no dependency, so it introduces no new supply-chain exposure; the standing gap (Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its transitive set never machine-checked against the NVD) belongs to CI or a human, not to this change.

The specialty query is uncached while the vet side reads the warm @Cacheable("vets") collection, and the whole table is read unpaged per request. At the demonstration's scale, and with NG-2 leaving no write path to grow the table, this is not a denial-of-service surface; it would become one only if a write path or a caller-supplied page size were ever added.
approved_aspects: No new trust boundary: GET /specialties.html takes no path variable, query parameter, request body, or header value. Nothing request-derived reaches the query, the read model, or the template, so the injection, mass-assignment, path-traversal, and cross-request-state rows of docs/security-principles.md are not engaged by this change.

Data access is a parameterless, constant JPQL string ('SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name') under @Query with @Transactional(readOnly = true). No concatenation, no user text; the ordering key is a literal, not a caller-supplied sort field, so no property-injection through ORDER BY.

Least privilege on the persistence surface holds as designed: SpecialtyRepository extends org.springframework.data.repository.Repository (a marker with no methods) and declares one read method. Verified by reading the interface and its imports — no save, delete, flush, or any other write method is exposed, so NG-2 is not widened. Basis: file read of SpecialtyRepository.java and its `extends` clause; no IDE oracle connected, so this is a text-level rather than symbol-resolved check.

Output escaping matches the codebase's single way of securing this concern. specialtyList.html renders stored specialty names and vet full names exclusively through th:text (Thymeleaf default escaping); no th:utext, no inline script, no external resource, no href on the new page, and no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) anywhere in the new template. It is line-for-line the vetList.html shape, including the #{none} empty cell, so no divergent escaping path is introduced.

The layout menu argument is the constant literal 'specialties'; the fragment uses `menu` only in an equality comparison for a CSS class, never in @{__${link}__} preprocessing, so the unmatched-menu technique adds no expression-evaluation surface.

Information exposure is not widened: specialty names and vet first/last names are already published by /vets.html and the serialized /vets route. The page adds a second view over the same data, not new data. No identifiers, no credentials, no internal detail reach the model or the page.

Fail-secure on missing data: SpecialtyDirectory.holds() treats a null specialty identifier as held-by-nobody rather than matching broadly, and matches on Integer identity via equals rather than object identity across the cached vet collection — an empty list is the failure mode, not a wrong or over-broad listing.

Concurrency: SpecialtyController is a singleton holding two final repository references and no mutable state; SpecialtyDirectory and its Entry are records whose compact constructors run List.copyOf, so the per-request read model is immutable and safe to share with the rendering thread. It only reads the @Cacheable vet collection and never mutates the cached entities.

No dependency, build, or configuration change: build.gradle, application*.properties, docker-compose.yml, and the Kubernetes manifest are untouched, so the supply chain and the credential baseline are unchanged by this slice. No hardcoded secret, token, key, or connection string appears in any added file — the only constants are test fixture names and message keys.

No dangerous-pattern hits across the vet package: no Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec, no Jackson polymorphic typing, no XML or YAML parsing, no filesystem writes, no java.util.Random, no System.out/System.err, no /tmp use. The one file read in the change set is the test's read-only Files.walk over src/main/resources/templates under try-with-resources with a fixed relative path.

Baseline comparison per docs/security-principles.md § Applying this section: the change introduces none of the table's vulnerability classes and leaves the application no weaker than the recorded baseline. The absence of authentication on the new route is NG-1 and the recorded posture in docs/system-design.md § Security Context, not a finding against this change.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Nine files in one module, 206 prod lines all purely additive (three new vet-package types plus one new template, zero deletions); the only edits to existing files are prose in docs/prd.md and docs/system-design.md. No sensitive path, no build.gradle, no schema, no seed data, no CacheConfiguration, no layout.html, no messages bundle, and VetController and its @WebMvcTest slice are untouched, so nothing already shipping changes behavior.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every hunk at the three risky coordinates the design block named and each behaves as documented: SpecialtyDirectory.holds matches on Integer identifier with an explicit null-id guard rather than object identity (correct, since BaseEntity defines no equals and the cached vets' Specialty instances are distinct objects), the listing is driven off SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties so a specialty nobody holds survives, and the empty-clinic path renders headers with an empty tbody. The JPQL is a constant parameterless string, ordering is explicit Comparators rather than HashSet iteration, the template uses only th:text with four message keys that already exist in messages.properties, and the layout menu argument matches no menu item so no navigation entry appears. Nothing inverted, nothing off-by-one, nothing wider than the prose claims.

test_adequacy.note: 611 test lines that would fail against a broken implementation, not restate it. The controller tests drive real Thymeleaf rendering through MockMvc and assert per-row containment via a row-splitting helper, so a vet named under the wrong specialty fails; the identifier-matching test builds separately-constructed Specialty instances sharing an id, which is exactly the bug the design block flagged and would catch an object-identity regression; edge cases 1 through 5 each have a dedicated case, immutability is asserted through UnsupportedOperationException, and the no-inbound-link requirement is checked by a real filesystem walk over every template rather than an allowlist. Doubles are hand-written, not Mockito.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four roster reviewers approved in round 2, but two approvals carry live caveats. The code-quality approval parks a declined round-1 recommendation in recommendations: multi-veterinarian cells render as an undelimited run-on because th:text bakes a trailing space into the name expression, so radiology reads as Helen Leary Linda Douglas with no separator. The dismissal cites vetList.html parity, and that basis is only partly right on my own read of both templates: vetList joins single-word specialty names, where a bare space is unambiguous, while this page joins two-word full names, where it is not, so the ambiguity is new here rather than inherited. The security approval separately states its supply-chain check was not run in either round and is not clean by assertion. Round 1 also carried three critical blocked doc findings and one fixable test-coverage finding; all four were fixed and re-approved, but that is a slice that needed a correction cycle.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions, and the prod diff sits exactly on the design block's primary paths. NG-2 holds structurally: SpecialtyRepository extends the bare Repository marker and declares one read method, so no write path was opened. Worth knowing rather than a deviation: the slice also amended an existing requirement, REQ-SYS-001, to record that navigation names two areas only and an unnamed page stays reachable, plus reworded the PRD provenance banner and dropped its open-question count.
